messages:
maria_support: heads up — AcmePay (INC-5342) just escalated: their SLAs triggered dozens of latency alerts around 09:00-09:15 UTC even though their traffic looks normal. customer says dashboards show 0 requests but alerts still firing. attaching screenshot: https://redwood.screenshots/acmepay/INC-5342.png

alex_reliability: thanks — can you paste the repro steps and the alert query? rough guess: aggregation window mismatch or using ingestion_time vs event_time.

maria_support: repro steps I used in Console -> Metrics: 1) Time range 08:55-09:20 UTC 2) query metric `api.request.count` grouped by 1m 3) alert threshold `rate(api.request.count[5m]) < 1` fired repeatedly. Raw events from the customer's logs show steady requests; dashboard raw-events query shows counts, but the precomputed chart shows blanks. Query I ran: ```SELECT count(*) as c, floor(event_ts/60000)*60000 as minute FROM api_requests WHERE customer_id='acmepay' AND event_ts BETWEEN 1670000000000 AND 1670000100000 GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute;```

sam_oncall: can you dump the aggregated rollups for the same window from the metrics-agg service? maybe rollup_interval is off or we shifted the bucket boundary. Also pinging metric-bot for any automated anomalies. @metric-bot status? :eyes:

metric-bot: auto: fetched rollups for customer acmepay, window 08:55-09:20 UTC. Found nulls at 09:03-09:07, rollup_interval=1m, last_ingest_time skew=+35s. (id: rb-agg-21)

alex_reliability: ok that log is useful. looks like the rollup pipeline is using ingestion_time to pick bucket boundaries instead of event_ts when event_ts < ingestion_time by >30s. code path in metrics-agg is doing `bucket = round(ingestion_time / 60000)` rather than `floor(event_ts / 60000)`. that would cause off-by-one buckets on late-arriving events -> empty buckets in precomputed chart -> threshold triggers on low-rate windows.

jessica_prod: confirming — there was a recent change in 2026-03-12 (PR #8421) that added a fast-path to use ingestion_time for 'fast ingest' mode. looks like we didn't backfill logic for late events. reproducer: take one event with event_ts = T and ingestion_time = T+45s; our aggregator currently places it in bucket(T+45s) which is the next minute. run the raw vs rollup diff and you'll see gaps.

alex_reliability: proposed mitigation: 1) patch aggregator to prefer event_ts when present: `bucket = floor(event_ts / 60000)` 2) deploy hotfix to metrics-agg in staging then prod (hotfix tag: fix/agg-eventtime-2026-03-17) 3) run a re-aggregation job for affected window (08:30-10:00 UTC) for AcmePay and any affected customers in the past 24h 4) temporarily suppress the specific alert rule for AcmePay until re-agg completes (or switch alert to use raw event query).

maria_support: customer-facing note ready: "We're investigating spurious alerts caused by a metrics aggregation boundary bug that can misplace late events into the wrong minute. We are deploying a fix and will reprocess last 1h of metrics; no data loss expected. ETA 1h." I'll send update to AcmePay ticket INC-5342.

sam_oncall: I'm running the hotfix now in staging, will smoke test against the repro steps. staging rollup log snippet: ```[2026-03-17T09:42:10Z] aggregator: bucket=1679090580000 event_ts=1679090525000 ingestion=1679090575000 -> corrected_bucket=1679090520000```

alex_reliability: once staging looks good, plan for prod: 1) deploy with 5-min maintenance window 2) run re-agg with idempotent job `reagg --customer acmepay --from 2026-03-17T08:30Z --to 2026-03-17T10:00Z` 3) revert alert suppression and monitor for 1 hour. I'll own the prod deploy.

jessica_prod: noted. I'll create the follow-up ops card and add postmortem template. action items: PATCH-8421 (code), JOB-989 (re-agg), TICKET-INC-5342 update. :white_check_mark: 

maria_support: thanks team — customer updated. closing loop after prod re-agg completes.

sam_oncall: staging tests passed, moving to prod in 10m. :rocket:
